name: Rob Kalin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Etsy in June 2005 at age 25, launching an online marketplace for handmade goods that grew into a multi-billion-dollar public company.
early_history_summary: Kalin grew up outside Boston with a teacher mother and architect father. His parents divorced, he was bullied in school, and he left home at 16 to work in a photo shop and live in an artist's squat. He attended five colleges, sneaking into MIT classes with fake IDs, before graduating from NYU's Gallatin School in 2004. He worked as a carpenter and woodworker, and the idea for Etsy emerged from his inability to sell his own handmade furniture online.
family_context_summary: Mother was a teacher, father was an architect. Parents divorced when Kalin was young; he left home at 16 and was largely self-supporting thereafter.
parent_family_domain_summary: Neither parent was directly involved in technology or e-commerce; father's architecture background may have influenced Kalin's maker/craft orientation.
evidence_summary: Kalin left home at 16 due to his parents' divorce and school bullying, supporting himself through odd jobs including carpentry and bookstore work. His direct experience as a woodworker unable to sell handmade furniture online was the catalyst for Etsy. He lacked programming skills but compensated by partnering with technical co-founders Chris Maguire and Haim Schoppik, whom he met through NYU and the GetCrafty.com project. The DIY/crafts movement and early e-commerce wave provided structural tailwinds.
starting_point: Born to a teacher mother and architect father outside Boston; parents divorced when he was young, and he left home at 16 to live independently.
current_position: Working on stealth AR/XR startup Dopple Works; previously built Catskill Mill artisan community and custom wooden loudspeakers in Catskill, NY; net worth not publicly reported.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Etsy in a Brooklyn apartment with Chris Maguire and Haim Schoppik, launching the online crafts marketplace.

Etsy went public via IPO, raising $237 million at $1.8 billion valuation.
Working on Dopple Works, a stealth handheld AR/XR device company.

name: Haim Schoppik
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Etsy in June 2005 at age 25 and served as its first CTO, building the initial platform's technical infrastructure.
early_history_summary: Schoppik attended Solomon Schechter Day School in New Jersey and worked at Goldman Sachs as a market data specialist (1999-2000) and Bridge Information Systems as a systems engineer (2000-2002) before attending NYU's Gallatin School from 2001 to 2005. He left NYU in 2005 as Etsy went live, having completed enough coursework to be considered an alumnus. His prior systems engineering experience at Goldman Sachs and Bridge Information Systems gave him the technical foundation to build Etsy's initial platform.
family_context_summary: Attended Solomon Schechter Day School of Essex and Union, a Jewish day school in New Jersey. Family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Schoppik brought real-world systems engineering experience from Goldman Sachs and Bridge Information Systems to the Etsy founding team, complementing Kalin's vision and Maguire's coding skills. His technical expertise in PostgreSQL, Linux, PHP, and OpenBSD was directly applicable to building Etsy's initial platform. The GetCrafty.com freelance project provided domain exposure to the crafts marketplace opportunity. He served as Etsy's CTO from 2005 to 2008 before leaving with Maguire.
starting_point: Attended Solomon Schechter Day School in New Jersey; worked at Goldman Sachs as a market data specialist at age 19 before attending NYU Gallatin.
current_position: Senior engineering leader based in Seattle; held CTO roles at Postling and Senior Director of Engineering at LocalVox after leaving Etsy in 2008.

name: Jack Abraham
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Milo.com in 2008 at age 22, a local product search engine that was acquired by eBay in December 2010 for approximately $75 million when he was 24.
early_history_summary: Abraham grew up in the Washington, D.C. area as the son of Magid Abraham, co-founder and CEO of comScore. He began programming at age 12 and working summers at comScore at age 13, where he fell in love with technology. In high school, he ran a custom-computer configuration company and a test-prep tutoring service. He enrolled at the Wharton School in 2004 to study technological entrepreneurship but dropped out in 2007 to found Milo.com, a local product search engine that indexed real-time store inventory.
family_context_summary: Son of Magid Abraham, co-founder and CEO of comScore, a global digital marketing intelligence company. Father grew up on a farm in Lebanon, earned a PhD from MIT, and founded multiple tech companies. Jack grew up with significant exposure to internet technology and entrepreneurship.
evidence_summary: Abraham's father co-founded and ran comScore, giving Jack direct exposure to internet analytics and e-commerce from age 12-13. He spent years working at comScore, ran businesses in high school, and designed his own major at Wharton before dropping out to found Milo. His father's network and resources provided significant early advantages, including investor connections and domain expertise in internet measurement. Milo was acquired by eBay for approximately $75 million in 2010, making him a successful exit founder by age 24.
starting_point: Born to Magid Abraham, co-founder and CEO of comScore, and grew up in the Washington, D.C. area with early and deep exposure to internet technology and entrepreneurship.
current_position: Founder and Managing Partner of Atomic, a startup studio and VC fund; co-founder of Hims & Hers Health and OpenStore; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.event: Founded Milo.com, a local product search engine indexing real-time store inventory, after dropping out of Wharton.

Atomic raised $260 million in additional funding; Hims & Hers went public via SPAC at a $1.6 billion valuation.

name: Travis Kalanick
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the Scour founding team in mid-1998 at age 22 and dropped out of UCLA to work full-time; Scour raised investment from former Disney president Michael Ovitz and became a high-profile P2P file-sharing company before facing a $250 billion lawsuit.
early_history_summary: Kalanick grew up in Northridge, Los Angeles, the son of a civil engineer father and retail advertising mother. He learned to code in middle school, sold Cutco knives door-to-door as a teenager, and started a test prep company at 18. He studied computer engineering at UCLA and joined the Scour founding team in 1998, dropping out to work full-time. After Scour's bankruptcy in 2000, he founded Red Swoosh, a P2P content delivery network sold to Akamai in 2007 for $23 million.
family_context_summary: Father was a civil engineer for the city of Los Angeles; mother worked in retail advertising for the Los Angeles Daily News. Middle-class suburban upbringing in Northridge, LA.
parent_family_domain_summary: Neither parent was in technology or internet; father's engineering background may have influenced early technical interest.
evidence_summary: Kalanick learned to code in middle school and demonstrated entrepreneurial drive early — selling Cutco knives and starting a test prep company at 18. At UCLA, he joined the Scour founding team of fellow CS students, dropping out to work full-time. The team of UCLA CS peers was the key early advantage, combined with riding the P2P/dot-com wave. His experience with Scour's lawsuits and investor disputes shaped his aggressive approach to business. No significant family financial or domain advantages were documented.
starting_point: Born in Northridge, Los Angeles, to a civil engineer father and retail advertising mother; middle-class suburban upbringing.
current_position: CEO of Atoms (formerly CloudKitchens/City Storage Systems), a robotics company in food, mining, and transport; net worth approximately $3.6 billion; resides in Austin, Texas.

name: Brian Armstrong
milestone_by_age_26: Founded UniversityTutor.com in 2003 at age 20 while studying at Rice University, building and running an online tutor-matching platform that grew to over 129,000 tutors across 125 countries and was eventually acquired in 2012.
early_history_summary: Armstrong grew up near San Jose, California, the son of two engineers. He attended Bellarmine College Preparatory, a private Catholic high school, then studied economics and computer science at Rice University, earning a dual BA in 2005 and an MS in computer science in 2006. While at Rice in 2003, he founded UniversityTutor.com, an online directory connecting students with tutors. After graduating, he spent a year in Buenos Aires, worked at IBM and Deloitte, then joined Airbnb as a software engineer in 2011 before co-founding Coinbase in 2012.
family_context_summary: Both parents were engineers. Grew up near San Jose, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley. Attended Bellarmine College Preparatory, a private Catholic high school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were engineers, providing a technical household environment, though not specifically in software or entrepreneurship.
evidence_summary: Armstrong demonstrated entrepreneurial drive early by founding UniversityTutor.com at age 20 while still at Rice University. Both parents were engineers and he grew up in Silicon Valley, providing a technical environment and geographic proximity to the tech industry. His university tutor-matching business was a modest but real venture that he ran for nearly a decade before co-founding Coinbase. The early evidence shows self-driven entrepreneurship rather than significant inherited advantages — he built his first company from scratch as a student.
starting_point: Born near San Jose, California, to two engineer parents; attended Bellarmine College Preparatory, a private Catholic high school, growing up in the heart of Silicon Valley.
current_position: Chairman and CEO of Coinbase, the largest U.S. cryptocurrency exchange; net worth approximately $7.7 billion; resides in San Francisco, California.

name: Fred Ehrsam
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Coinbase in 2012 at age 24 with Brian Armstrong, building what became the largest U.S. cryptocurrency exchange; served as its first President.
early_history_summary: Ehrsam grew up in Concord, Massachusetts, and attended Concord-Carlisle High School. He became an avid competitive World of Warcraft player in high school, spending thousands of hours exploring its in-game economy, which introduced him to digital currency concepts. He graduated from Duke University with a BS in Computer Science and Economics (Latin honors, departmental distinction), then worked as a foreign exchange trader at Goldman Sachs from 2010 to 2012. He met Brian Armstrong through the Bitcoin subreddit and co-founded Coinbase in 2012.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Concord, Massachusetts, an affluent Boston suburb. Family financial background not specifically documented, but Concord is among the most affluent towns in the state.
evidence_summary: Ehrsam's path to Coinbase was shaped by elite institutional training — Duke University with Latin honors and departmental distinction, followed by FX trading at Goldman Sachs — giving him deep financial markets expertise and technical skills. His thousands of hours in World of Warcraft's virtual economy provided early intuition for digital currencies. He met Brian Armstrong through the Bitcoin subreddit, forming a complementary team that rode the crypto wave at its inception. His Goldman Sachs salary provided modest capital safety, and his FX trading gave direct domain exposure to currency markets that translated to crypto.
starting_point: Born in Boston and raised in Concord, Massachusetts, an affluent suburb; attended Concord-Carlisle High School where he became a competitive World of Warcraft player.
current_position: Co-founder and Senior Advisor at Paradigm (crypto VC managing ~$13B); co-founder and CEO of Nudge (neurotech startup); net worth approximately $3.1 billion.
